# ===== vllm/core/swa_ring.py =====
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
"""SWA ring buffer (VLLM_NEURON_SWA_RING=1) for sliding-window KV groups.

Each sliding-window (SWA) KV group of a request keeps a fixed ring of
``ring_blocks = cdiv(window, block_size)`` blocks. The ring is the first
``ring_blocks`` blocks that vLLM allocated to the request for that group, in
block-table order. For Gemma3 (window 1024, block 32) the ring has 32 blocks and
``ring_slots = 1024`` slots.

Ring modulus
------------
The decode kernel (nkilib ``attention_tkg``) always places the K/V of the
active token at the last table slot ``s_prior - 1``. The decode mask also marks
that slot as the active slot. The ring therefore reserves the last slot. A
position ``p`` maps to the ring slot ``p % R`` with ``R = ring_slots - 1``
(1023 for Gemma3). The ``R`` ring slots then hold exactly the prior window
``[p - R, p - 1]`` at decode position ``p``. Gemma3 attends ``k >= p - 1023``,
so ``R = window - 1`` is sufficient when ``ring_slots == window``.

The write of position ``p`` overwrites the slot of position ``p - R``. The
decode step reads the cache before it writes it (the in-kernel update runs after
the attention, and the external scatter runs after the layer loop). Position
``p - R`` is inside the window of ``p``, so the step reads it first and then
replaces it.

Decode mask
-----------
Prior slot ``s`` is valid if ``s < min(p, R)``. Before the ring is full the
valid slots are ``[0, p)``, which is the linear layout. After that every ring
slot is valid. Pass ``pos_ids = min(p, R)`` and ``start_pos = 0``.

Prefill
-------
Prefill writes only the last ``R`` positions of the prompt to the ring, at
``p % R``. All earlier positions go to the null block. Single-shot prefill
attends the raw K/V, so it never reads this layout. Segmented prefill and
prefix caching read the linear layout, so the ring refuses them.

Block management
----------------
vLLM's ``SlidingWindowManager`` allocates blocks for the whole sequence and
frees out-of-window head blocks (``remove_skipped_blocks``). The ring blocks are
those head blocks, so the scheduler must keep them. ``RingSlidingWindowManager``
below replaces the SWA manager when the ring is on:

* ``get_num_skipped_tokens`` returns 0, so vLLM never frees a ring block, and
  ``remove_skipped_blocks`` frees nothing.
* ``get_num_blocks_to_allocate`` / ``allocate_new_blocks`` clamp the request to
  ``hold_blocks = ring_blocks + 1`` blocks (33 for Gemma3). The ring uses only
  the first ``ring_blocks`` blocks. The extra block is the "+1" of the planned
  admission charge (6 x 33 + full); it is held but not written.

A request then holds at most ``hold_blocks`` blocks for each SWA group, in both
the prefill phase and the decode phase. Admission charges exactly that.

This module imports nothing from vLLM at module level, so the arithmetic can be
checked on any CPU.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np


def cdiv(a: int, b: int) -> int:
    return -(-a // b)


def ring_blocks(sliding_window: int, block_size: int) -> int:
    """Blocks in the ring of one SWA group.

    Example:
        >>> ring_blocks(1024, 32)
        32
    """
    return cdiv(sliding_window, block_size)


def ring_slots(sliding_window: int, block_size: int) -> int:
    """Slots in the ring table (the decode ``s_prior``).

    Example:
        >>> ring_slots(1024, 32)
        1024
    """
    return ring_blocks(sliding_window, block_size) * block_size


def ring_modulus(sliding_window: int, block_size: int) -> int:
    """Ring modulus R. The last table slot is kept for the active token.

    Example:
        >>> ring_modulus(1024, 32)
        1023
    """
    return ring_slots(sliding_window, block_size) - 1


def hold_blocks(sliding_window: int, block_size: int) -> int:
    """Blocks one request holds for one SWA group when the ring is on.

    Example:
        >>> hold_blocks(1024, 32)
        33
    """
    return ring_blocks(sliding_window, block_size) + 1


def check_ring_geometry(sliding_window: int, block_size: int) -> None:
    """Raise if the ring cannot hold the full window.

    The ring holds R = ring_slots - 1 prior tokens. The model attends the
    window - 1 prior tokens, so R must be at least window - 1.
    """
    R = ring_modulus(sliding_window, block_size)
    if R < sliding_window - 1:
        raise ValueError(
            f"SWA ring modulus {R} is smaller than window - 1 ({sliding_window - 1}). "
            "Use a block size that divides the sliding window."
        )


def ring_slot_mapping(
    positions: np.ndarray,
    req_indices: np.ndarray,
    block_table: np.ndarray,
    block_size: int,
    sliding_window: int,
    null_slot: int = 0,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Map the SWA positions of one step to ring slots in the paged cache.

    In one step each request keeps only its last R positions; earlier positions
    of the same step go to ``null_slot``. A single-shot prefill of L tokens then
    writes ``[L - R, L)`` and a decode step writes its one token. Distinct kept
    positions of one request never share a ring slot.

    Args:
        positions: Absolute token positions, one per scheduled token.
        req_indices: Row in ``block_table`` for each token.
        block_table: Raw host block table of the SWA group [rows, width].
        block_size: Tokens per block.
        sliding_window: Window of the group.
        null_slot: Discard slot (vLLM null block 0).

    Returns:
        int64 slot per token.

    Example:
        >>> bt = np.arange(1, 41).reshape(1, 40)
        >>> ring_slot_mapping(np.array([1023]), np.array([0]), bt, 32, 1024).tolist()
        [32]
    """
    R = ring_modulus(sliding_window, block_size)
    nb = ring_blocks(sliding_window, block_size)
    positions = np.asarray(positions, dtype=np.int64)
    req_indices = np.asarray(req_indices, dtype=np.int64)
    if positions.size == 0:
        return positions.copy()
    assert block_table.shape[1] >= nb, (block_table.shape, nb)
    r = positions % R
    blocks = block_table[req_indices, r // block_size].astype(np.int64)
    slots = blocks * block_size + (r % block_size)
    # Step end per request: keep [end - R, end).
    end = np.zeros(int(req_indices.max()) + 1, dtype=np.int64)
    np.maximum.at(end, req_indices, positions + 1)
    drop = positions < end[req_indices] - R
    # A ring block that is still the null block (not allocated) also discards.
    drop |= blocks == 0
    return np.where(drop, null_slot, slots)


def ring_table(block_table: np.ndarray, sliding_window: int, block_size: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Fixed decode table: the first ``ring_blocks`` columns of the block table.

    Example:
        >>> ring_table(np.arange(80).reshape(2, 40), 1024, 32).shape
        (2, 32)
    """
    return block_table[:, : ring_blocks(sliding_window, block_size)]


def ring_mask_pos(positions: np.ndarray, sliding_window: int, block_size: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Decode-mask end position: prior slot s is valid iff s < min(p, R).

    Example:
        >>> ring_mask_pos(np.array([0, 5, 1023, 4000]), 1024, 32).tolist()
        [0, 5, 1023, 1023]
    """
    return np.minimum(np.asarray(positions), ring_modulus(sliding_window, block_size))


def ring_hold_blocks_for_tokens(num_tokens: int, sliding_window: int, block_size: int) -> int:
    """Blocks the ring manager lets a request hold for ``num_tokens`` tokens.

    Example:
        >>> ring_hold_blocks_for_tokens(2050, 1024, 32)
        33
        >>> ring_hold_blocks_for_tokens(100, 1024, 32)
        4
    """
    return min(cdiv(num_tokens, block_size), hold_blocks(sliding_window, block_size))


def make_ring_manager_class(base_cls):
    """Return a SlidingWindowManager subclass that keeps a fixed ring per request.

    ``base_cls`` is vLLM's ``SlidingWindowManager``. The import stays in the
    caller so this module has no vLLM import.
    """

    class RingSlidingWindowManager(base_cls):
        """SWA manager for VLLM_NEURON_SWA_RING=1.

        Holds at most ``ring_blocks + 1`` blocks per request and never frees a
        block before the request ends. The model runner maps every position to
        a ring slot inside the first ``ring_blocks`` blocks.
        """

        def __init__(self, kv_cache_spec, **kwargs) -> None:
            super().__init__(kv_cache_spec, **kwargs)
            check_ring_geometry(kv_cache_spec.sliding_window, self.block_size)
            self._ring_hold = hold_blocks(kv_cache_spec.sliding_window, self.block_size)
            cap = self._max_admission_blocks_per_request
            self._max_admission_blocks_per_request = (
                self._ring_hold if cap is None else min(cap, self._ring_hold)
            )

        def get_num_skipped_tokens(self, num_computed_tokens: int) -> int:
            # The ring reuses the head blocks. Nothing is out of the window.
            return 0

        def remove_skipped_blocks(
            self, request_id, processed_computed_tokens, num_prompt_tokens=None
        ) -> None:
            return None

        def get_num_blocks_to_allocate(
            self,
            request_id,
            num_tokens,
            new_computed_blocks,
            total_computed_tokens,
            num_local_computed_tokens,
            num_tokens_main_model,
            apply_admission_cap=False,
        ) -> int:
            num_tokens = min(num_tokens, self._ring_hold * self.block_size)
            return super().get_num_blocks_to_allocate(
                request_id,
                num_tokens,
                new_computed_blocks,
                total_computed_tokens,
                num_local_computed_tokens,
                min(num_tokens_main_model, num_tokens),
                apply_admission_cap=apply_admission_cap,
            )

        def allocate_new_blocks(self, request_id, num_tokens, num_tokens_main_model):
            num_tokens = min(num_tokens, self._ring_hold * self.block_size)
            return super().allocate_new_blocks(
                request_id, num_tokens, min(num_tokens_main_model, num_tokens)
            )

        def cache_blocks(self, request, num_tokens, retention_interval=None) -> None:
            # Ring blocks are rewritten in place, so they are never a valid prefix hit.
            return None

    return RingSlidingWindowManager


def install_ring_managers(kv_cache_manager) -> int:
    """Swap every plain SlidingWindowManager of ``kv_cache_manager`` for the ring one.

    Call this right after the KV cache manager is built, before any request.

    Returns:
        Number of managers that were replaced.
    """
    from vllm.v1.core.single_type_kv_cache_manager import SlidingWindowManager

    ring_cls = make_ring_manager_class(SlidingWindowManager)
    n = 0
    for m in kv_cache_manager.coordinator.single_type_managers:
        if type(m) is SlidingWindowManager:
            assert not m.req_to_blocks, "install the SWA ring before the first request"
            m.__class__ = ring_cls
            check_ring_geometry(m.sliding_window, m.block_size)
            m._ring_hold = hold_blocks(m.sliding_window, m.block_size)
            cap = m._max_admission_blocks_per_request
            m._max_admission_blocks_per_request = (
                m._ring_hold if cap is None else min(cap, m._ring_hold)
            )
            n += 1
    return n


# ===== vllm/core/kv_admission.py =====
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
"""Real-usage KV admission bound for hybrid sliding-window / full-attention models.

vLLM's per-request capacity (``get_max_concurrency_for_kv_cache_config``) charges
every sliding-window (SWA) group
``cdiv(min(window - 1 + max_concurrent_batches * max_num_batched_tokens,
max_model_len), block_size) + 1`` blocks. Under async scheduling (K = 2) with a
large ``max_num_batched_tokens`` this is the full ``max_model_len``, so a SWA group
is charged like a full-attention group.

What a request really holds, given vLLM 0.29's block manager
(``KVCacheManager.allocate_slots`` frees out-of-window SWA blocks on the
processed-token basis, ``max(0, computed - in_flight)``, before every allocation):

* Every group holds at most ``cdiv(computed + new + lookahead, block_size)`` blocks
  (blocks are a prefix of the sequence, minus the freed ones).
* Before its first post-prefill allocation (prefill phase, including the time a
  finished prefill sits hidden while the Neuron scheduler runs other prefills),
  computed + new <= P + K * d, where P is the prompt length and d the tokens per
  decode step. This is the *prefill-phase* bound.
* Afterwards a SWA group holds at most the window, the trailing retained tokens and
  the unprocessed + newly scheduled tokens (<= K * d), +1 block because the window
  need not start on a block boundary; a full-attention group grows to
  ``cdiv(min(P + M + K * d, max_model_len), block_size)``. This is the
  *decode-phase* bound.

The SWA groups shrink before the full-attention group grows, so the per-request
peak is ``max(prefill-phase total, decode-phase total)``, not the sum of per-group
maxima. If the scheduler admits only while the sum of these peaks over all live
requests fits the usable pool, no ``allocate_slots`` call can fail, so no request
is preempted.

With VLLM_NEURON_SWA_EARLY_FREE=1 the scheduler frees a request's out-of-window
SWA blocks as soon as its prefill output is processed (instead of at its first
decode allocation, which the Neuron scheduler can postpone for many steps while it
hides decodes behind other prefills), and from then on charges that request only
the decode-phase bound (``phase_charge``). With N live requests of which k_p are
still in the prefill phase, admission is then
``(N - k_p) * decode + k_p * prefill <= usable``.

This module imports nothing from vLLM so the arithmetic can be checked on any CPU.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass


def cdiv(a: int, b: int) -> int:
    return -(-a // b)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class GroupDesc:
    """One KV cache group, reduced to what the bound needs.

    kind: "swa" (plain sliding window) or "full" (holds every block until the
        request finishes).
    upstream_blocks: vLLM's per-request block charge for the group
        (``cdiv(spec.max_memory_usage_bytes(cfg), spec.page_size_bytes)``); the real
        bound is clamped to it, so it can never exceed the upstream charge.
    ring_blocks: VLLM_NEURON_SWA_RING only (0 = off). A "swa" group then holds at
        most this many blocks in every phase (``swa_ring.hold_blocks``) and frees
        none before the request ends.
    """

    kind: str
    block_size: int
    upstream_blocks: int
    sliding_window: int = 0
    extra_retained_tokens: int = 0
    ring_blocks: int = 0


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AdmissionParams:
    groups: tuple
    num_blocks: int
    usable_blocks: int
    max_model_len: int
    max_concurrent_batches: int
    decode_tokens: int
    lookahead_tokens: int

    @property
    def upstream_blocks_per_request(self) -> int:
        return sum(g.upstream_blocks for g in self.groups)

    @property
    def legacy_cap(self) -> int:
        w = self.upstream_blocks_per_request
        return self.num_blocks // w if w > 0 else 0


def make_params(
    groups,
    num_blocks: int,
    max_model_len: int,
    max_concurrent_batches: int,
    decode_tokens: int = 1,
    lookahead_tokens: int = 0,
    watermark_blocks: int = 0,
) -> AdmissionParams:
    # One block of the pool is vLLM's null block; the watermark is kept free.
    return AdmissionParams(
        groups=tuple(groups),
        num_blocks=num_blocks,
        usable_blocks=num_blocks - 1 - watermark_blocks,
        max_model_len=max_model_len,
        max_concurrent_batches=max(1, max_concurrent_batches),
        decode_tokens=max(1, decode_tokens),
        lookahead_tokens=max(0, lookahead_tokens),
    )


def _in_flight(p: AdmissionParams) -> int:
    return p.max_concurrent_batches * p.decode_tokens + p.lookahead_tokens


def prefill_phase_blocks(p: AdmissionParams, prefill_len: int) -> int:
    tokens = min(prefill_len + _in_flight(p), p.max_model_len)
    total = 0
    for g in p.groups:
        blocks = cdiv(tokens, g.block_size)
        if g.kind == "swa" and g.ring_blocks:
            blocks = min(blocks, g.ring_blocks)
        total += min(blocks, g.upstream_blocks)
    return total


def decode_phase_blocks(p: AdmissionParams, final_len: int) -> int:
    full_tokens = min(final_len + _in_flight(p), p.max_model_len)
    total = 0
    for g in p.groups:
        if g.kind == "swa" and g.ring_blocks:
            # Ring: the group holds its first ring_blocks blocks to the end.
            blocks = min(cdiv(full_tokens, g.block_size), g.ring_blocks)
        elif g.kind == "swa":
            swa_tokens = min(
                g.sliding_window - 1 + g.extra_retained_tokens + _in_flight(p),
                full_tokens,
            )
            blocks = cdiv(swa_tokens, g.block_size) + 1
        else:
            blocks = cdiv(full_tokens, g.block_size)
        total += min(blocks, g.upstream_blocks)
    return total


def request_peak_blocks(p: AdmissionParams, prefill_len: int, final_len: int) -> int:
    """Upper bound on the blocks one request holds at any time, all groups.

    prefill_len: tokens its (next) prefill covers -- the prompt, or every token
        so far for a preempted request that must re-prefill.
    final_len: prompt + max_tokens (clamped to max_model_len inside).
    """
    return max(prefill_phase_blocks(p, prefill_len), decode_phase_blocks(p, final_len))


def phase_charge(
    p: AdmissionParams, prefill_len: int, final_len: int, swa_freed: bool
) -> int:
    """Admission charge for one request, by phase (VLLM_NEURON_SWA_EARLY_FREE).

    swa_freed: the request's prefill output has been processed, no prefill
        tokens are still in flight, and its out-of-window SWA blocks were freed
        right away (``NeuronScheduler._swa_early_free``). From then on it never
        holds more than the decode-phase bound, so that is its charge. Otherwise
        the charge is the unchanged ``request_peak_blocks``.
    """
    if swa_freed:
        return decode_phase_blocks(p, final_len)
    return request_peak_blocks(p, prefill_len, final_len)


def uniform_cap(p: AdmissionParams, prompt_len: int, max_tokens: int) -> int:
    """Concurrent requests of one shape that fit the usable pool (log / tests)."""
    w = request_peak_blocks(p, prompt_len, prompt_len + max_tokens)
    return p.usable_blocks // w if w > 0 else 0

"""
Mellum Config
=============

Checkpoint: ``JetBrains/Mellum2.1-12B-A2.5B-Thinking`` (and the Mellum2 family):
``model_type: mellum``, ``architectures: ["MellumForCausalLM"]``.

Architecture (verified against config.json and transformers' ``modular_mellum.py``):

  hidden 2304 / 28 layers / 32 Q heads / 4 KV heads / head_dim 128 / vocab 98304 /
  RMSNorm eps 1e-6 (gamma * norm(x)) / per-head QK-norm before RoPE / no bias /
  untied LM head.
  Attention schedule: ``layer_types`` = [sliding x3, full] x7, sliding window 1024.
  RoPE per layer type (``rope_parameters`` is NESTED by layer type):
    sliding_attention: default, theta 5e5
    full_attention:    yarn, theta 5e5, factor 16, original_max_position_embeddings 8192,
                       beta_fast 32, beta_slow 1, attention_factor 1.2773
  MLP: sparse MoE in every layer (``mlp_layer_types``): 64 experts, top-8, softmax router
  in fp32, renormalized top-k (``norm_topk_prob``), SiLU GLU, moe_intermediate_size 896,
  no shared expert.

Config parsing traps handled here:
  * ``rope_parameters`` is a dict of dicts keyed by layer type. A flat parse (or vLLM's
    ``MellumConfig(Qwen3MoeConfig)`` shim) injects a flat ``rope_theta`` of 1e4 and drops the
    YaRN parameters. ``from_configs`` reads both sub-dicts explicitly and ``validate`` asserts
    the result.
  * ``num_experts`` is stored as ``num_local_experts`` by transformers' attribute map.
"""

import json
import math
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

import torch
from transformers import PretrainedConfig

from vllm_neuron.model.neuron_config import NeuronConfig

_SLIDING = "sliding_attention"
_FULL = "full_attention"


@dataclass
class MellumConfig:
    # <-- MODEL-SPECIFIC: architecture
    vocab_size: int = 98304
    hidden_size: int = 2304
    intermediate_size: int = 7168  # dense MLP size (unused: every layer is sparse)
    num_hidden_layers: int = 28
    num_attention_heads: int = 32
    num_key_value_heads: int = 4
    head_dim: int | None = 128
    max_position_embeddings: int = 131072
    rms_norm_eps: float = 1e-6
    attention_bias: bool = False
    hidden_act: str = "silu"
    tie_word_embeddings: bool = False

    # Hybrid attention schedule
    sliding_window: int = 1024
    layer_types: list[str] | None = None

    # MoE
    num_experts: int = 64
    num_experts_per_tok: int = 8
    moe_intermediate_size: int = 896
    norm_topk_prob: bool = True
    mlp_layer_types: list[str] | None = None

    # RoPE per layer type (parsed from the nested rope_parameters)
    rope_parameters: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    sliding_rope_theta: float = 500000.0
    full_rope_theta: float = 500000.0
    full_rope_type: str = "default"
    full_rope_factor: float = 1.0
    full_rope_original_max_position: int | None = None
    full_rope_beta_fast: float = 32.0
    full_rope_beta_slow: float = 1.0
    full_rope_attention_factor: float = 1.0
    full_rope_truncate: bool = True

    torch_dtype: torch.dtype = torch.bfloat16
    neuron_config: NeuronConfig | None = None

    def __post_init__(self):
        if self.head_dim is None:
            self.head_dim = self.hidden_size // self.num_attention_heads
        if self.layer_types is None:
            self.layer_types = [_FULL] * self.num_hidden_layers
        if self.mlp_layer_types is None:
            self.mlp_layer_types = ["sparse"] * self.num_hidden_layers
        self.validate()

    # Attributes the shared Gemma3 attention module reads.
    @property
    def query_pre_attn_scalar(self) -> float:
        # Mellum uses the standard head_dim ** -0.5 softmax scale.
        return float(self.head_dim)

    def is_sliding(self, layer_idx: int) -> bool:
        return self.layer_types[layer_idx] == _SLIDING

    def validate(self) -> None:
        """Load-time config assert: fail on a mis-parsed config instead of running wrong."""
        assert self.num_attention_heads % self.num_key_value_heads == 0
        assert self.head_dim % 2 == 0
        assert len(self.layer_types) == self.num_hidden_layers, (
            f"layer_types has {len(self.layer_types)} entries, num_hidden_layers={self.num_hidden_layers}"
        )
        unknown = set(self.layer_types) - {_SLIDING, _FULL}
        assert not unknown, f"unknown layer_types values: {sorted(unknown)}"
        assert len(self.mlp_layer_types) == self.num_hidden_layers
        if any(t != "sparse" for t in self.mlp_layer_types):
            raise NotImplementedError(
                "Mellum on Neuron implements sparse MoE layers only; the checkpoint has "
                f"mlp_layer_types={sorted(set(self.mlp_layer_types))}."
            )
        assert self.num_experts_per_tok <= self.num_experts
        assert self.full_rope_type in ("default", "yarn"), (
            f"full_attention rope_type {self.full_rope_type!r} is not implemented"
        )
        if self.full_rope_type == "yarn":
            assert self.full_rope_factor > 1.0 and self.full_rope_original_max_position, (
                "yarn RoPE needs factor > 1 and original_max_position_embeddings"
            )
        if self.attention_bias:
            raise NotImplementedError("attention_bias=True is not implemented for Mellum on Neuron")
        if self.hidden_act != "silu":
            raise NotImplementedError(f"hidden_act={self.hidden_act!r} is not implemented")

    def summary(self) -> str:
        return (
            f"layers={self.num_hidden_layers} sliding={sum(self.is_sliding(i) for i in range(self.num_hidden_layers))} "
            f"window={self.sliding_window} heads={self.num_attention_heads}/{self.num_key_value_heads} d={self.head_dim} "
            f"experts={self.num_experts} top{self.num_experts_per_tok} I={self.moe_intermediate_size} "
            f"norm_topk={self.norm_topk_prob} rope sliding theta={self.sliding_rope_theta} full {self.full_rope_type} "
            f"theta={self.full_rope_theta} factor={self.full_rope_factor} orig={self.full_rope_original_max_position} "
            f"attn_factor={self.full_rope_attention_factor:.6f}"
        )

    @classmethod
    def from_configs(cls, hf_config: PretrainedConfig, neuron_config: NeuronConfig | None = None):
        if isinstance(hf_config, (str, bytes)):
            with open(hf_config) as f:
                d = json.load(f)
        elif isinstance(hf_config, PretrainedConfig):
            d = hf_config.to_dict()
            dt = getattr(hf_config, "torch_dtype", None) or getattr(hf_config, "dtype", None)
            if dt is not None:
                d["torch_dtype"] = dt
        else:
            d = dict(hf_config)

        d = dict(d)
        if "num_experts" not in d and "num_local_experts" in d:
            d["num_experts"] = d["num_local_experts"]
        if d.get("torch_dtype") is None and d.get("dtype") is not None:
            d["torch_dtype"] = d["dtype"]

        d.update(cls._parse_rope(d))
        # Reduced-layer bring-up (hf_overrides num_hidden_layers < checkpoint): keep the schedule prefix.
        n = d.get("num_hidden_layers")
        for key in ("layer_types", "mlp_layer_types"):
            if isinstance(d.get(key), list) and n is not None and len(d[key]) > n:
                d[key] = d[key][:n]

        names = {f.name for f in cls.__dataclass_fields__.values()}
        kw = {k: v for k, v in d.items() if k in names}
        if isinstance(kw.get("torch_dtype"), str):
            kw["torch_dtype"] = getattr(torch, kw["torch_dtype"])
        if kw.get("torch_dtype") is None:
            kw.pop("torch_dtype", None)
        kw["neuron_config"] = neuron_config
        return cls(**kw)

    @staticmethod
    def _parse_rope(d: dict) -> dict:
        """Read the nested per-layer-type rope_parameters into flat fields."""
        rp = d.get("rope_parameters")
        if not isinstance(rp, dict) or not rp:
            raise ValueError("Mellum config has no rope_parameters")
        if _SLIDING not in rp and _FULL not in rp:
            raise ValueError(
                "Mellum rope_parameters must be nested by layer type "
                f"({_SLIDING!r}, {_FULL!r}); got keys {sorted(rp)}"
            )
        s = rp.get(_SLIDING) or rp.get(_FULL)
        f = rp.get(_FULL) or rp.get(_SLIDING)
        if s.get("rope_type", "default") != "default":
            raise NotImplementedError(f"sliding rope_type {s.get('rope_type')!r} is not implemented")
        out = {
            "sliding_rope_theta": float(s["rope_theta"]),
            "full_rope_theta": float(f["rope_theta"]),
            "full_rope_type": f.get("rope_type", "default"),
        }
        if out["full_rope_type"] == "yarn":
            factor = float(f["factor"])
            out.update(
                full_rope_factor=factor,
                full_rope_original_max_position=int(f["original_max_position_embeddings"]),
                full_rope_beta_fast=float(f.get("beta_fast") or 32.0),
                full_rope_beta_slow=float(f.get("beta_slow") or 1.0),
                full_rope_truncate=bool(f.get("truncate", True)),
            )
            af = f.get("attention_factor")
            if af is None:
                # transformers' default (no mscale fields): 0.1 * ln(factor) + 1
                af = 0.1 * math.log(factor) + 1.0 if factor > 1 else 1.0
            out["full_rope_attention_factor"] = float(af)
        return out

"""
Mellum BF16 Implementation
==========================

Mellum (``MellumForCausalLM``, e.g. ``JetBrains/Mellum2.1-12B-A2.5B-Thinking``) for the Neuron
backend. Supported parallelism: TP, SP (prefill), optional EP for the experts, DP.

Architecture = Qwen3-MoE attention + MoE with a hybrid sliding-window schedule:

  * GQA 32 Q / 4 KV heads, head_dim 128, per-head QK RMSNorm BEFORE RoPE, no bias.
  * 3 sliding-window (1024) layers then 1 full-attention layer, repeated.
  * RoPE per layer type: sliding = default theta 5e5; full = YaRN (factor 16, original 8192,
    attention_factor 1.2773 multiplied into cos/sin, as in transformers).
  * Every layer is a sparse MoE: 64 experts, top-8, softmax in fp32, renormalized top-k,
    SiLU GLU, no shared expert.
  * Pre-norm residual blocks (input_layernorm -> attn, post_attention_layernorm -> MoE).
    RMSNorm is ``w * norm(x)`` (no Gemma-style ``1 + w``).

Reused from ``model/gemma3`` (same branch): the attention module (QK-norm + per-layer sliding
window in prefill and in the fused decode kernel), the two-mask decode precompute with the SWA
``swa_kv_pos_offset`` rebase, and the deferred / coalesced KV write-back. The SWA scheduler
features (``VLLM_NEURON_SWA_*``) are model independent and apply here too.

ANNOTATION GUIDE:
  # >>> PARALLELISM: ... <<<   Reusable parallelism code.
  # <-- MODEL-SPECIFIC: ...    Mellum-specific.

MODEL ENV GATES (read at trace time; Dynamo folds them):
  MELLUM_MOE_DECODE   "auto" (default): fp32 router, then the routed-expert gather when
                      T * top_k <= local experts, else every local expert on every token ("dense").
                      "gather" / "dense" force one; "kernel": fused moe_block_tkg (bf16 router;
                      needs I/rank % 128 == 0).
  MELLUM_MOE_PREFILL  "auto" (default): blockwise moe_cte kernel when I/rank % 128 == 0 (EP4 on one
                      device), else the dense torch MoE. "kernel" / "torch" force a path.
  MELLUM_DECODE_ATTN  "stock" (default): fused attention_block_tkg decode kernel.
                      "torch": the plugin's torch reference of the same kernel.
"""

# =============================================================================
# Section 1: RMSNorm
# <-- MODEL-SPECIFIC: transformers' MellumRMSNorm normalizes in fp32, casts to the input dtype,
#     THEN multiplies by the weight: ``w * norm(x).to(dtype)``.
# =============================================================================


class MellumRMSNorm(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, hidden_size: int, eps: float, dtype: torch.dtype):
        super().__init__()
        self.weight = nn.Parameter(torch.ones(hidden_size, dtype=dtype))
        self.variance_epsilon = eps

    def forward(self, hidden_states: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        input_dtype = hidden_states.dtype
        h = hidden_states.to(torch.float32)
        h = h * torch.rsqrt(h.pow(2).mean(-1, keepdim=True) + self.variance_epsilon)
        return self.weight * h.to(input_dtype)


# =============================================================================
# Section 2: RoPE per layer type (default on sliding layers, YaRN on full layers)
# Computed lazily in forward (the model is built on the meta device).
# =============================================================================


def _yarn_inv_freq(config: MellumConfig, device) -> torch.Tensor:
    """transformers ``_compute_yarn_parameters`` (inverse frequencies only)."""
    dim = config.head_dim
    base = config.full_rope_theta
    factor = config.full_rope_factor
    orig = config.full_rope_original_max_position

    def corr_dim(num_rot):
        return (dim * math.log(orig / (num_rot * 2 * math.pi))) / (2 * math.log(base))

    low, high = corr_dim(config.full_rope_beta_fast), corr_dim(config.full_rope_beta_slow)
    if config.full_rope_truncate:
        low, high = math.floor(low), math.ceil(high)
    low, high = max(low, 0), min(high, dim - 1)
    if low == high:
        high += 0.001
    pos_freqs = base ** (torch.arange(0, dim, 2, dtype=torch.float, device=device) / dim)
    inv_extra = 1.0 / pos_freqs
    inv_inter = 1.0 / (factor * pos_freqs)
    ramp = torch.clamp(
        (torch.arange(dim // 2, dtype=torch.float32, device=device) - low) / (high - low), 0, 1
    )
    extra_factor = 1 - ramp
    return inv_inter * (1 - extra_factor) + inv_extra * extra_factor


class MellumRotaryEmbedding(nn.Module):
    """Returns ``{"sliding": (cos, sin), "global": (cos, sin)}`` (keys used by the Gemma3 backbone code)."""

    def __init__(self, config: MellumConfig):
        super().__init__()
        self.config = config
        self.head_dim = config.head_dim
        self.full_scale = float(config.full_rope_attention_factor) if config.full_rope_type == "yarn" else 1.0

    def _inv_freq(self, kind: str, device) -> torch.Tensor:
        c = self.config
        if kind == "global" and c.full_rope_type == "yarn":
            return _yarn_inv_freq(c, device)
        base = c.full_rope_theta if kind == "global" else c.sliding_rope_theta
        return 1.0 / (base ** (torch.arange(0, self.head_dim, 2, dtype=torch.float, device=device) / self.head_dim))

    def _cos_sin(self, kind, position_ids, device, dtype, scale):
        inv = self._inv_freq(kind, device)
        freqs = (inv[:, None].float() @ position_ids[None, :].float()).transpose(0, 1)
        emb = torch.cat((freqs, freqs), dim=-1)
        cos, sin = emb.cos(), emb.sin()
        if scale != 1.0:
            cos, sin = cos * scale, sin * scale
        return cos.to(dtype), sin.to(dtype)

    def forward(self, position_ids, device, dtype):
        return {
            "sliding": self._cos_sin("sliding", position_ids, device, dtype, 1.0),
            "global": self._cos_sin("global", position_ids, device, dtype, self.full_scale),
        }

# Section 4: Sparse MoE (64 experts, top-8, softmax + renorm, SiLU GLU, no shared expert)
# =============================================================================


def _per_expert_gate_up_loader(
    intermediate: int, hidden: int, i_tp: int, num_shards: int, hidden_padded: int, i_padded: int
):
    """``[gate_0..gate_{E-1}, up_0..up_{E-1}]`` each ``[I, H]`` -> ``[E, Hp, 2 * Ip]`` (gate slice first; H and I_tp zero-padded)."""

    def transform(slices, rank):
        n = len(slices) // 2
        start = (rank % num_shards) * i_tp
        out = []
        for e in range(n):
            g, u = slices[e], slices[n + e]
            for s in (g, u):
                if tuple(s.get_shape()) != (intermediate, hidden):
                    raise ValueError(f"expert gate/up shape {list(s.get_shape())} != [{intermediate}, {hidden}]")
            gs, us = g[start : start + i_tp, :], u[start : start + i_tp, :]
            if i_padded > i_tp:
                gs = torch.nn.functional.pad(gs, (0, 0, 0, i_padded - i_tp))
                us = torch.nn.functional.pad(us, (0, 0, 0, i_padded - i_tp))
            w = torch.cat([gs, us], dim=0).t()
            if hidden_padded > hidden:
                w = torch.nn.functional.pad(w, (0, 0, 0, hidden_padded - hidden))
            out.append(w)
        return torch.stack(out, 0).contiguous()

    return SafetensorsWeightLoader(transform=transform)


def _per_expert_down_loader(
    intermediate: int, hidden: int, i_tp: int, num_shards: int, hidden_padded: int, i_padded: int
):
    """``[down_0..down_{E-1}]`` each ``[H, I]`` -> ``[E, Ip, Hp]`` (H and I_tp zero-padded)."""

    def transform(slices, rank):
        start = (rank % num_shards) * i_tp
        out = []
        for s in slices:
            if tuple(s.get_shape()) != (hidden, intermediate):
                raise ValueError(f"expert down shape {list(s.get_shape())} != [{hidden}, {intermediate}]")
            w = s[:, start : start + i_tp].t()
            if hidden_padded > hidden or i_padded > i_tp:
                w = torch.nn.functional.pad(w, (0, hidden_padded - hidden, 0, i_padded - i_tp))
            out.append(w)
        return torch.stack(out, 0).contiguous()

    return SafetensorsWeightLoader(transform=transform)


class MellumSparseMoeBlock(nn.Module):
    """Router + routed experts. Owns post_attention_layernorm (the decode kernel fuses it).

    >>> PARALLELISM <<<
    - No EP: every rank holds all experts; TP shards the expert intermediate size.
    - EP (``--enable-expert-parallel``): EP rank k holds experts [k*E_L, (k+1)*E_L); the EP-TP
      sub-group shards the intermediate size.
    - Prefill is sequence parallel: all-gather tokens -> experts -> reduce-scatter.
    - Decode: every rank has all tokens -> partial outputs -> all-reduce.
    """

    def __init__(self, config: MellumConfig):
        super().__init__()
        self.tp_group = get_tp_group()
        self.world_size = self.tp_group.world_size

        from vllm.config import get_current_vllm_config

        pc = get_current_vllm_config().parallel_config
        ep_enabled = pc.enable_expert_parallel
        if ep_enabled and pc.data_parallel_size > 1:
            raise NotImplementedError("Mellum: expert parallelism across data-parallel replicas is not implemented")
        from vllm_neuron.parallel.neuron_parallel_state import (
            get_neuron_ep_degree,
            get_neuron_ep_rank,
            get_neuron_ep_tp_group,
        )

        self.ep_degree = get_neuron_ep_degree() if ep_enabled else 1
        if self.ep_degree > 1:
            self.ep_rank = get_neuron_ep_rank()
            self.ep_tp_group = get_neuron_ep_tp_group()
        else:
            self.ep_rank = 0
            self.ep_tp_group = self.tp_group
        self.tp_degree = self.ep_tp_group.world_size

        self.num_experts = config.num_experts
        self.top_k = config.num_experts_per_tok
        self.norm_topk_prob = config.norm_topk_prob
        self.hidden_size = config.hidden_size
        self.intermediate_size = config.moe_intermediate_size
        self.rms_norm_eps = config.rms_norm_eps
        self.dtype = config.torch_dtype
        if self.num_experts % self.ep_degree:
            raise ValueError(f"num_experts {self.num_experts} not divisible by EP degree {self.ep_degree}")
        if self.intermediate_size % self.tp_degree:
            raise ValueError(f"moe_intermediate_size {self.intermediate_size} not divisible by MoE TP {self.tp_degree}")
        if not self.norm_topk_prob:
            raise NotImplementedError("Mellum on Neuron implements norm_topk_prob=True routing only")
        self.num_local_experts = self.num_experts // self.ep_degree
        self.i_tp = self.intermediate_size // self.tp_degree
        self.block_size = 256
        # The prefill expert kernel (bwmm) tiles H by 512 (H=2304 is not a multiple). Like gpt_oss, keep the
        # experts zero-padded to Hp inside the MoE block only; the residual stream stays at H.
        # MELLUM_MOE_PAD_H=0 keeps H unpadded (then prefill must use MELLUM_MOE_PREFILL=torch).
        pad = os.environ.get("MELLUM_MOE_PAD_H", "1") == "1"
        self.hp = ((self.hidden_size + _H_ALIGN - 1) // _H_ALIGN) * _H_ALIGN if pad else self.hidden_size
        # MELLUM_MOE_PAD_I=1: zero-pad the expert width per rank to a multiple of 128 (exact: silu(0) * 0 = 0).
        # Off by default: it adds decode bytes and did not fix the TP-sharded prefill kernel issue below.
        self.i_real = self.i_tp
        if os.environ.get("MELLUM_MOE_PAD_I", "0") == "1" and self.i_tp % _DECODE_KERNEL_I_ALIGNMENT:
            self.i_tp = ((self.i_tp + _DECODE_KERNEL_I_ALIGNMENT - 1) // _DECODE_KERNEL_I_ALIGNMENT) * _DECODE_KERNEL_I_ALIGNMENT

        self.post_attention_layernorm = MellumRMSNorm(self.hidden_size, self.rms_norm_eps, self.dtype)
        # >>> PARALLELISM: router replicated on every rank <<<
        self.router_weight = nn.Parameter(torch.empty(self.num_experts, self.hidden_size, dtype=self.dtype))
        self.gate_up_proj_weight = nn.Parameter(
            torch.empty(self.num_local_experts, self.hp, 2 * self.i_tp, dtype=self.dtype)
        )
        self.down_proj_weight = nn.Parameter(
            torch.empty(self.num_local_experts, self.i_tp, self.hp, dtype=self.dtype)
        )

        gu = _per_expert_gate_up_loader(
            self.intermediate_size, self.hidden_size, self.i_real, self.tp_degree, self.hp, self.i_tp
        )
        dn = _per_expert_down_loader(
            self.intermediate_size, self.hidden_size, self.i_real, self.tp_degree, self.hp, self.i_tp
        )
        if self.ep_degree > 1:
            local = list(range(self.ep_rank * self.num_local_experts, (self.ep_rank + 1) * self.num_local_experts))
            gu = expert_parallel_grouped_loader(local, gu, self.num_experts)
            dn = expert_parallel_grouped_loader(local, dn, self.num_experts)
        set_weight_loader(self.gate_up_proj_weight, gu)
        set_weight_loader(self.down_proj_weight, dn)

    # ── helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def _ep_rank_tensor(self):
        from vllm_neuron.parallel.neuron_parallel_state import get_neuron_ep_group

        return get_neuron_ep_group().rank_in_group_tensor

    def _decode_weights(self, path: str):
        """Expert weights for the torch decode paths, without the zero H padding when that is faster.

        MELLUM_MOE_DECODE_HSLICE: "auto" (default) slices H for the dense path only; "1" / "0" force it.
        Measured on trn2 (EP4, TP4): dense at batch 64 2,728 tok/s sliced vs 1,980 padded; the gather at
        batch 1 36 tok/s sliced (index_select over a non-contiguous view) vs 103 padded.
        """
        hs = os.environ.get("MELLUM_MOE_DECODE_HSLICE", "auto")
        use = (path == "dense") if hs == "auto" else hs == "1"
        if self.hp > self.hidden_size and use:
            return self.gate_up_proj_weight[:, : self.hidden_size, :], self.down_proj_weight[..., : self.hidden_size], False
        return self.gate_up_proj_weight, self.down_proj_weight, True

    def _pad_h(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        return torch.nn.functional.pad(x, (0, self.hp - self.hidden_size)) if self.hp > self.hidden_size else x

    def _unpad_h(self, y: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        return y[..., : self.hidden_size] if self.hp > self.hidden_size else y

    def _route(self, x: torch.Tensor):
        """fp32 logits -> softmax -> top-k -> renorm. Returns (weights fp32 [T,k], ids [T,k])."""
        probs = torch.softmax(x.float() @ self.router_weight.float().T, dim=-1)
        topv, topi = torch.topk(probs, self.top_k, dim=-1)
        if self.norm_topk_prob:
            topv = topv / topv.sum(-1, keepdim=True)
        return topv, topi

    def _decode_mode(self, T: int) -> str:
        # Default "gather": fp32 router + routed experts only. The fused kernel ("kernel") computes the router
        # logits in bf16 (an fp32 router input fails its dtype check) and failed the fp32 first-divergence
        # gate on trn2 (gap 0.40 / 1.05 vs <= 0.23 for gather at the same EP4 layout); it also needs
        # I/rank % 128 == 0 (EP4 on one device).
        # "auto": the gather reads T * top_k expert slices, the dense path reads each local expert once.
        mode = os.environ.get("MELLUM_MOE_DECODE", "auto")
        if mode == "auto":
            return "gather" if T * self.top_k <= self.num_local_experts else "dense"
        return mode

    # ── forward ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def forward(
        self,
        hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
        is_decode: bool,
        positions: torch.Tensor | None = None,
        segmented: bool = False,
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        hidden_states = hidden_states.to(self.dtype)
        if is_decode:
            mode = self._decode_mode(hidden_states.shape[0])
            if mode == "kernel":
                out = self._unpad_h(self._decode_kernel(hidden_states))
            elif mode == "dense":
                out = self._decode_dense(hidden_states)
            else:
                out = self._decode_gather(hidden_states)
            if self.world_size > 1:
                out = self.tp_group.all_reduce(out)
            return out
        return self._prefill(hidden_states, positions, segmented)

    def _decode_kernel(self, hidden_states):
        """Fused RMSNorm + router + all local experts (nkilib moe_block_tkg)."""
        if can_run_kernel(hidden_states) and self.i_tp % _DECODE_KERNEL_I_ALIGNMENT:
            raise ValueError(
                f"moe_block_tkg needs the per-rank expert intermediate size ({self.i_tp}) to be a multiple of "
                f"{_DECODE_KERNEL_I_ALIGNMENT}. Enable expert parallelism or use MELLUM_MOE_DECODE=gather."
            )
        rank_id = (
            self._ep_rank_tensor().reshape(1, 1).to(torch.int32)
            if self.ep_degree > 1
            else torch.zeros((1, 1), dtype=torch.int32, device=hidden_states.device)
        )
        return NF.moe_block_tkg(
            inp=self._pad_h(hidden_states).unsqueeze(0),
            gamma=self._pad_h(self.post_attention_layernorm.weight).unsqueeze(0).to(torch.float32),
            router_weights=self._pad_h(self.router_weight).T,
            expert_gate_up_weights=self.gate_up_proj_weight.reshape(self.num_local_experts, self.hp, 2, self.i_tp),
            expert_down_weights=self.down_proj_weight,
            rank_id=rank_id,
            top_k=self.top_k,
            eps=self.rms_norm_eps,
            # <-- MODEL-SPECIFIC: give every routing argument (the wrapper defaults are SIGMOID / no renorm).
            router_act_fn=RouterActFnType.SOFTMAX,
            router_pre_norm=True,  # softmax before top-k (not the RMSNorm)
            norm_topk_prob=self.norm_topk_prob,
            expert_affinities_scaling_mode=ExpertAffinityScaleMode.POST_SCALE,
            hidden_act_fn=ActFnType.SiLU,
            router_mm_dtype=nl.bfloat16,
            hidden_actual=self.hidden_size,  # RMSNorm over the real H, not the padded Hp
            is_all_expert=True,
            skip_router_logits=True,
        )

    def _local_route(self, topv, topi):
        """With EP: keep only this rank's experts (others get weight 0, slot 0)."""
        if self.ep_degree == 1:
            return topv, topi
        lo = self._ep_rank_tensor().to(topi.dtype) * self.num_local_experts
        local = topi - lo
        mine = (local >= 0) & (local < self.num_local_experts)
        return torch.where(mine, topv, torch.zeros_like(topv)), torch.where(mine, local, torch.zeros_like(local))

    def _decode_gather(self, hidden_states):
        """Read only the T * top_k routed expert slices (index_select, chunked)."""
        x = self.post_attention_layernorm(hidden_states)
        T = x.shape[0]
        topv, topi = self._local_route(*self._route(x))
        w_gu, w_dn, padded = self._decode_weights("gather")
        if padded:
            x = self._pad_h(x)
        hx = x.shape[-1]
        idx = topi.reshape(-1)
        n = T * self.top_k
        xr = x.unsqueeze(1).expand(T, self.top_k, hx).reshape(n, 1, hx)
        ys = []
        for c0 in range(0, n, _GATHER_CHUNK):
            c1 = min(c0 + _GATHER_CHUNK, n)
            ic = idx[c0:c1]
            gu = torch.bmm(xr[c0:c1], w_gu.index_select(0, ic))
            h = torch.nn.functional.silu(gu[..., : self.i_tp]) * gu[..., self.i_tp :]
            ys.append(torch.bmm(h, w_dn.index_select(0, ic)))
        y = (torch.cat(ys, 0) if len(ys) > 1 else ys[0]).reshape(T, self.top_k, hx)
        out = (y.float() * topv.unsqueeze(-1)).sum(1).to(self.dtype)
        return self._unpad_h(out) if padded else out

    def _dense(self, x, topv, topi):
        """Every local expert on every token, weighted by the (local) affinity."""
        T = x.shape[0]
        aff = torch.zeros(T, self.num_experts, dtype=torch.float32, device=x.device).scatter(1, topi, topv)
        if self.ep_degree > 1:
            lo = self._ep_rank_tensor().to(torch.long) * self.num_local_experts
            cols = torch.arange(self.num_local_experts, device=x.device, dtype=torch.long) + lo
            aff = aff.index_select(1, cols)
        w_gu, w_dn, padded = self._decode_weights("dense")
        gu = torch.einsum("th,ehi->eti", self._pad_h(x) if padded else x, w_gu)
        h = torch.nn.functional.silu(gu[..., : self.i_tp]) * gu[..., self.i_tp :]
        y = torch.einsum("eti,eih->eth", h, w_dn)
        out = (y.float() * aff.t().unsqueeze(-1)).sum(0).to(self.dtype)
        return self._unpad_h(out) if padded else out

    def _decode_dense(self, hidden_states):
        x = self.post_attention_layernorm(hidden_states)
        topv, topi = self._route(x)
        return self._dense(x, topv, topi)

    def _prefill(self, hidden_states, positions=None, segmented=False):
        """SP shard -> norm + router -> all-gather -> experts -> reduce-scatter."""
        x = self.post_attention_layernorm(hidden_states)
        # The blockwise kernel gave wrong prefill output on trn2 at TP4 without EP (experts' I sharded 4 ways,
        # I/rank 224, also with I zero-padded to 256) under segmented prefill with 1,024-token chunks. It passed
        # single-shot prefill at the same layout, and every case with whole experts per rank (EP4). "auto" uses
        # the kernel unless the experts are I-sharded AND the prefill is segmented.
        mode = os.environ.get("MELLUM_MOE_PREFILL", "auto")
        if mode == "auto":
            mode = "torch" if (self.tp_degree > 1 and segmented) else "kernel"
        if mode == "torch":
            topv, topi = self._route(x)
            if self.world_size > 1:
                x = self.tp_group.all_gather(x, dim=0)
                topv = self.tp_group.all_gather(topv, dim=0)
                topi = self.tp_group.all_gather(topi, dim=0)
            out = self._dense(x, topv, topi)
            if self.world_size > 1:
                out = self.tp_group.reduce_scatter(out, dim=0)
            return out

        if os.environ.get("MELLUM_MOE_ROUTER", "kernel") == "torch":
            topv, topi = self._route(x)
            aff = torch.zeros(x.shape[0], self.num_experts, dtype=torch.float32, device=x.device).scatter(1, topi, topv)
        else:
          aff = NF.router(
            hidden_states=x,
            router_weights=self.router_weight.T,
            top_k=self.top_k,
            activation="softmax",
            computation_dtype=torch.float32,
            router_computation_order=RouterComputationOrder.PRENORM_LINEAR_ACT_TOPK_RENORM_SCATTER,
          )
        if self.world_size > 1:
            aff = self.tp_group.all_gather(aff, dim=0)
            x = self.tp_group.all_gather(x, dim=0)
        # Padding rows (after the last real token) take no expert blocks (gpt_oss pattern). Positions are
        # increasing over the real tokens of a single-request prefill chunk and zero-padded after them.
        padding_mask = None
        if positions is not None and os.environ.get("MELLUM_MOE_PAD_MASK", "1") == "1":
            pos = positions.reshape(-1)
            last_real = torch.argmax(pos)
            padding_mask = torch.arange(pos.shape[0], device=pos.device) <= last_real
        if self.ep_degree > 1:
            ep_rank = self._ep_rank_tensor().to(torch.int32)
            local_ids = torch.arange(self.num_local_experts, device=x.device, dtype=torch.int32) + (
                ep_rank * self.num_local_experts
            )
            aff = NF.get_local_expert_affinities(aff, local_ids)
        aff_masked, tok_pos_to_id, block_to_expert, conditions = NF.build_blockwise_mapping(
            expert_affinities=aff,
            num_local_experts=self.num_local_experts,
            num_experts_per_token=self.top_k,
            block_size=self.block_size,
            moe_group=self.ep_tp_group,
            tp_degree=self.tp_degree,
            padding_mask=padding_mask,
        )
        out = NF.moe_cte(
            implementation=MoECTEImplementation.shard_on_block,
            conditions=conditions,
            hidden_states=self._pad_h(x),
            expert_affinities_masked=aff_masked,
            gate_up_proj_weight=self.gate_up_proj_weight.reshape(self.num_local_experts, self.hp, 2, self.i_tp),
            down_proj_weight=self.down_proj_weight,
            activation_function=ActFnType.SiLU,
            block_size=self.block_size,
            token_position_to_id=tok_pos_to_id.to(dtype=torch.int32),
            block_to_expert=block_to_expert.to(dtype=torch.int32),
            expert_affinities_scaling_mode=ExpertAffinityScaleMode.POST_SCALE,
            skip_token=True,
            is_tensor_update_accumulating=True,
            compute_dtype=nl.bfloat16,
        )
        out = self._unpad_h(out)
        if self.world_size > 1:
            out = self.tp_group.reduce_scatter(out, dim=0)
        return out


# =============================================================================
# Section 5: Decoder layer (pre-norm; the MoE block applies post_attention_layernorm)
# =============================================================================


class MellumDecoderLayer(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, config: MellumConfig, layer_idx: int):
        super().__init__()
        self.input_layernorm = MellumRMSNorm(config.hidden_size, config.rms_norm_eps, config.torch_dtype)
        self.self_attn = MellumAttention(config, layer_idx=layer_idx)
        self.mlp = MellumSparseMoeBlock(config)
        self.layer_idx = layer_idx

    def forward(self, hidden_states, positions, position_embeddings, attn_mask=None, attn_metadata=None, kv_writeback=None):
        m = attn_metadata[f"layers.{self.layer_idx}.self_attn"]
        is_decode = m["max_query_len"] <= m["decode_token_threshold"]
        residual = hidden_states
        hidden_states = self.self_attn(
            hidden_states=self.input_layernorm(hidden_states),
            positions=positions,
            position_embeddings=position_embeddings,
            attn_mask=attn_mask,
            attn_metadata=attn_metadata,
            kv_writeback=kv_writeback,
        )
        hidden_states = residual + hidden_states
        segmented = bool(m.get("kv_segment_size"))
        return hidden_states + self.mlp(hidden_states, is_decode=is_decode, positions=positions, segmented=segmented)

# Section 6: Backbone (Gemma3 backbone flow without the embedding scale)
# =============================================================================


class MellumModel(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, config: MellumConfig):
        super().__init__()
        self.config = config
        self.tp_group = get_tp_group()
        self.world_size = self.tp_group.world_size
        self.rank = self.tp_group.rank_in_group
        self.kv_ptr_group_of = None
        self.embed_tokens = VocabDimShardedEmbedding(
            vocab_size=config.vocab_size,
            embed_dim=config.hidden_size,
            dtype=config.torch_dtype,
            tp_group=self.tp_group.device_group,
        )
        self.layers = nn.ModuleList([MellumDecoderLayer(config, i) for i in range(config.num_hidden_layers)])
        self.norm = MellumRMSNorm(config.hidden_size, config.rms_norm_eps, config.torch_dtype)
        self.rotary_emb = MellumRotaryEmbedding(config)
        self.sliding_probe_layer, self.global_probe_layer = _resolve_schedule_probe_layers(config)
        set_weight_loader(
            self.embed_tokens.weight,
            sharding_weight_loader(
                shard_dim=0,
                shard_size=self.embed_tokens.vocab_size_per_rank,
                num_shards=self.world_size,
                is_storage_transposed=False,
                pad_shard=True,
            ),
        )

    def forward(self, input_ids, positions, attn_metadata=None, rank=None, inputs_embeds=None, is_token_ids=None):
        m0 = attn_metadata["layers.0.self_attn"]
        is_prefill = m0["max_query_len"] > m0["decode_token_threshold"]

        hidden_states = self.embed_tokens(input_ids, scatter_tokens=is_prefill, rank=rank)
        if is_prefill and self.world_size > 1 and inputs_embeds is not None and is_token_ids is not None:
            n = hidden_states.shape[0]
            inputs_embeds = inputs_embeds[self.rank * n : (self.rank + 1) * n]
            is_token_ids = is_token_ids[self.rank * n : (self.rank + 1) * n]
        hidden_states = NF.merge_prompt_embeds(hidden_states, inputs_embeds, is_token_ids)

        rope = self.rotary_emb(positions, device=hidden_states.device, dtype=hidden_states.dtype)

        sliding_mask = global_mask = None
        if not is_prefill:
            sliding_mask, global_mask = _precompute_decode_attn_masks(
                config=self.config,
                attn_metadata=attn_metadata,
                positions=positions,
                num_q_heads_per_rank=self.layers[0].self_attn.num_attention_heads_per_rank,
                sliding_probe_layer=self.sliding_probe_layer,
                global_probe_layer=self.global_probe_layer,
            )

        # Deferred + coalesced KV write-back (see gemma3 model "X5"). Prefill defers only on the
        # single-shot path (enforced per layer in forward_prefill).
        if is_prefill:
            coalesce = os.environ.get("GEMMA3_PREFILL_KV_COALESCE", "1") == "1"
        else:
            coalesce = os.environ.get("GEMMA3_KV_COALESCE", "1") == "1"
        kv_writeback = [] if coalesce else None
        if not is_prefill:
            attn_metadata["_g3_kv_chain"] = {}

        for layer in self.layers:
            sliding = layer.self_attn.is_sliding
            hidden_states = layer(
                hidden_states,
                positions=positions,
                position_embeddings=rope["sliding" if sliding else "global"],
                attn_mask=sliding_mask if sliding else global_mask,
                attn_metadata=attn_metadata,
                kv_writeback=kv_writeback,
            )

        if not is_prefill:
            attn_metadata.pop("_g3_kv_chain", None)
        if kv_writeback:
            _coalesce_kv_writes(kv_writeback, self.kv_ptr_group_of)

        hidden_states = self.norm(hidden_states)
        if is_prefill and self.world_size > 1:
            hidden_states = self.tp_group.all_gather(hidden_states, dim=0)
        return hidden_states, []

        unexpected = [k for k in (result.unexpected_keys or []) if not _ignored(k)]
        if missing or unexpected:

                f"Mellum weights do not match the checkpoint: missing params {missing[:10]} ({len(missing)}), "
                f"unused checkpoint keys {unexpected[:10]} ({len(unexpected)})"

        sd = result.state_dict
        for k, t in sd.items():
            if t.dtype != self.config.torch_dtype:
                sd[k] = t.to(self.config.torch_dtype)
        self.load_state_dict(sd, strict=False, assign=True)

# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
"""SWA ring buffer (VLLM_NEURON_SWA_RING=1) for sliding-window KV groups.

Each sliding-window (SWA) KV group of a request keeps a fixed ring of
``ring_blocks = cdiv(window, block_size)`` blocks. The ring is the first
``ring_blocks`` blocks that vLLM allocated to the request for that group, in
block-table order. For Gemma3 (window 1024, block 32) the ring has 32 blocks and
``ring_slots = 1024`` slots.

Ring modulus
------------
The decode kernel (nkilib ``attention_tkg``) always places the K/V of the
active token at the last table slot ``s_prior - 1``. The decode mask also marks
that slot as the active slot. The ring therefore reserves the last slot. A
position ``p`` maps to the ring slot ``p % R`` with ``R = ring_slots - 1``
(1023 for Gemma3). The ``R`` ring slots then hold exactly the prior window
``[p - R, p - 1]`` at decode position ``p``. Gemma3 attends ``k >= p - 1023``,
so ``R = window - 1`` is sufficient when ``ring_slots == window``.

The write of position ``p`` overwrites the slot of position ``p - R``. The
decode step reads the cache before it writes it (the in-kernel update runs after
the attention, and the external scatter runs after the layer loop). Position
``p - R`` is inside the window of ``p``, so the step reads it first and then
replaces it.

Decode mask
-----------
Prior slot ``s`` is valid if ``s < min(p, R)``. Before the ring is full the
valid slots are ``[0, p)``, which is the linear layout. After that every ring
slot is valid. Pass ``pos_ids = min(p, R)`` and ``start_pos = 0``.

Prefill
-------
Prefill writes only the last ``R`` positions of the prompt to the ring, at
``p % R``. All earlier positions go to the null block. Single-shot prefill
attends the raw K/V, so it never reads this layout. Segmented prefill and
prefix caching read the linear layout, so the ring refuses them.

Block management
----------------
vLLM's ``SlidingWindowManager`` allocates blocks for the whole sequence and
frees out-of-window head blocks (``remove_skipped_blocks``). The ring blocks are
those head blocks, so the scheduler must keep them. ``RingSlidingWindowManager``
below replaces the SWA manager when the ring is on:

* ``get_num_skipped_tokens`` returns 0, so vLLM never frees a ring block, and
  ``remove_skipped_blocks`` frees nothing.
* ``get_num_blocks_to_allocate`` / ``allocate_new_blocks`` clamp the request to
  ``hold_blocks = ring_blocks + 1`` blocks (33 for Gemma3). The ring uses only
  the first ``ring_blocks`` blocks. The extra block is the "+1" of the planned
  admission charge (6 x 33 + full); it is held but not written.

A request then holds at most ``hold_blocks`` blocks for each SWA group, in both
the prefill phase and the decode phase. Admission charges exactly that.

This module imports nothing from vLLM at module level, so the arithmetic can be
checked on any CPU.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np


def cdiv(a: int, b: int) -> int:
    return -(-a // b)


def ring_blocks(sliding_window: int, block_size: int) -> int:
    """Blocks in the ring of one SWA group.

    Example:
        >>> ring_blocks(1024, 32)
        32
    """
    return cdiv(sliding_window, block_size)


def ring_slots(sliding_window: int, block_size: int) -> int:
    """Slots in the ring table (the decode ``s_prior``).

    Example:
        >>> ring_slots(1024, 32)
        1024
    """
    return ring_blocks(sliding_window, block_size) * block_size


def ring_modulus(sliding_window: int, block_size: int) -> int:
    """Ring modulus R. The last table slot is kept for the active token.

    Example:
        >>> ring_modulus(1024, 32)
        1023
    """
    return ring_slots(sliding_window, block_size) - 1


def hold_blocks(sliding_window: int, block_size: int) -> int:
    """Blocks one request holds for one SWA group when the ring is on.

    Example:
        >>> hold_blocks(1024, 32)
        33
    """
    return ring_blocks(sliding_window, block_size) + 1


def check_ring_geometry(sliding_window: int, block_size: int) -> None:
    """Raise if the ring cannot hold the full window.

    The ring holds R = ring_slots - 1 prior tokens. The model attends the
    window - 1 prior tokens, so R must be at least window - 1.
    """
    R = ring_modulus(sliding_window, block_size)
    if R < sliding_window - 1:
        raise ValueError(
            f"SWA ring modulus {R} is smaller than window - 1 ({sliding_window - 1}). "
            "Use a block size that divides the sliding window."
        )


def ring_slot_mapping(
    positions: np.ndarray,
    req_indices: np.ndarray,
    block_table: np.ndarray,
    block_size: int,
    sliding_window: int,
    null_slot: int = 0,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Map the SWA positions of one step to ring slots in the paged cache.

    In one step each request keeps only its last R positions; earlier positions
    of the same step go to ``null_slot``. A single-shot prefill of L tokens then
    writes ``[L - R, L)`` and a decode step writes its one token. Distinct kept
    positions of one request never share a ring slot.

    Args:
        positions: Absolute token positions, one per scheduled token.
        req_indices: Row in ``block_table`` for each token.
        block_table: Raw host block table of the SWA group [rows, width].
        block_size: Tokens per block.
        sliding_window: Window of the group.
        null_slot: Discard slot (vLLM null block 0).

    Returns:
        int64 slot per token.

    Example:
        >>> bt = np.arange(1, 41).reshape(1, 40)
        >>> ring_slot_mapping(np.array([1023]), np.array([0]), bt, 32, 1024).tolist()
        [32]
    """
    R = ring_modulus(sliding_window, block_size)
    nb = ring_blocks(sliding_window, block_size)
    positions = np.asarray(positions, dtype=np.int64)
    req_indices = np.asarray(req_indices, dtype=np.int64)
    if positions.size == 0:
        return positions.copy()
    assert block_table.shape[1] >= nb, (block_table.shape, nb)
    r = positions % R
    blocks = block_table[req_indices, r // block_size].astype(np.int64)
    slots = blocks * block_size + (r % block_size)
    # Step end per request: keep [end - R, end).
    end = np.zeros(int(req_indices.max()) + 1, dtype=np.int64)
    np.maximum.at(end, req_indices, positions + 1)
    drop = positions < end[req_indices] - R
    # A ring block that is still the null block (not allocated) also discards.
    drop |= blocks == 0
    return np.where(drop, null_slot, slots)


def ring_table(block_table: np.ndarray, sliding_window: int, block_size: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Fixed decode table: the first ``ring_blocks`` columns of the block table.

    Example:
        >>> ring_table(np.arange(80).reshape(2, 40), 1024, 32).shape
        (2, 32)
    """
    return block_table[:, : ring_blocks(sliding_window, block_size)]


def ring_mask_pos(positions: np.ndarray, sliding_window: int, block_size: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Decode-mask end position: prior slot s is valid iff s < min(p, R).

    Example:
        >>> ring_mask_pos(np.array([0, 5, 1023, 4000]), 1024, 32).tolist()
        [0, 5, 1023, 1023]
    """
    return np.minimum(np.asarray(positions), ring_modulus(sliding_window, block_size))


def ring_hold_blocks_for_tokens(num_tokens: int, sliding_window: int, block_size: int) -> int:
    """Blocks the ring manager lets a request hold for ``num_tokens`` tokens.

    Example:
        >>> ring_hold_blocks_for_tokens(2050, 1024, 32)
        33
        >>> ring_hold_blocks_for_tokens(100, 1024, 32)
        4
    """
    return min(cdiv(num_tokens, block_size), hold_blocks(sliding_window, block_size))


def make_ring_manager_class(base_cls):
    """Return a SlidingWindowManager subclass that keeps a fixed ring per request.

    ``base_cls`` is vLLM's ``SlidingWindowManager``. The import stays in the
    caller so this module has no vLLM import.
    """

    class RingSlidingWindowManager(base_cls):
        """SWA manager for VLLM_NEURON_SWA_RING=1.

        Holds at most ``ring_blocks + 1`` blocks per request and never frees a
        block before the request ends. The model runner maps every position to
        a ring slot inside the first ``ring_blocks`` blocks.
        """

        def __init__(self, kv_cache_spec, **kwargs) -> None:
            super().__init__(kv_cache_spec, **kwargs)
            check_ring_geometry(kv_cache_spec.sliding_window, self.block_size)
            self._ring_hold = hold_blocks(kv_cache_spec.sliding_window, self.block_size)
            cap = self._max_admission_blocks_per_request
            self._max_admission_blocks_per_request = (
                self._ring_hold if cap is None else min(cap, self._ring_hold)
            )

        def get_num_skipped_tokens(self, num_computed_tokens: int) -> int:
            # The ring reuses the head blocks. Nothing is out of the window.
            return 0

        def remove_skipped_blocks(
            self, request_id, processed_computed_tokens, num_prompt_tokens=None
        ) -> None:
            return None

        def get_num_blocks_to_allocate(
            self,
            request_id,
            num_tokens,
            new_computed_blocks,
            total_computed_tokens,
            num_local_computed_tokens,
            num_tokens_main_model,
            apply_admission_cap=False,
        ) -> int:
            num_tokens = min(num_tokens, self._ring_hold * self.block_size)
            return super().get_num_blocks_to_allocate(
                request_id,
                num_tokens,
                new_computed_blocks,
                total_computed_tokens,
                num_local_computed_tokens,
                min(num_tokens_main_model, num_tokens),
                apply_admission_cap=apply_admission_cap,
            )

        def allocate_new_blocks(self, request_id, num_tokens, num_tokens_main_model):
            num_tokens = min(num_tokens, self._ring_hold * self.block_size)
            return super().allocate_new_blocks(
                request_id, num_tokens, min(num_tokens_main_model, num_tokens)
            )

        def cache_blocks(self, request, num_tokens, retention_interval=None) -> None:
            # Ring blocks are rewritten in place, so they are never a valid prefix hit.
            return None

    return RingSlidingWindowManager


def install_ring_managers(kv_cache_manager) -> int:
    """Swap every plain SlidingWindowManager of ``kv_cache_manager`` for the ring one.

    Call this right after the KV cache manager is built, before any request.

    Returns:
        Number of managers that were replaced.
    """
    from vllm.v1.core.single_type_kv_cache_manager import SlidingWindowManager

    ring_cls = make_ring_manager_class(SlidingWindowManager)
    n = 0
    for m in kv_cache_manager.coordinator.single_type_managers:
        if type(m) is SlidingWindowManager:
            assert not m.req_to_blocks, "install the SWA ring before the first request"
            m.__class__ = ring_cls
            check_ring_geometry(m.sliding_window, m.block_size)
            m._ring_hold = hold_blocks(m.sliding_window, m.block_size)
            cap = m._max_admission_blocks_per_request
            m._max_admission_blocks_per_request = (
                m._ring_hold if cap is None else min(cap, m._ring_hold)
            )
            n += 1
    return n

# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
"""Real-usage KV admission bound for hybrid sliding-window / full-attention models.

vLLM's per-request capacity (``get_max_concurrency_for_kv_cache_config``) charges
every sliding-window (SWA) group
``cdiv(min(window - 1 + max_concurrent_batches * max_num_batched_tokens,
max_model_len), block_size) + 1`` blocks. Under async scheduling (K = 2) with a
large ``max_num_batched_tokens`` this is the full ``max_model_len``, so a SWA group
is charged like a full-attention group.

What a request really holds, given vLLM 0.29's block manager
(``KVCacheManager.allocate_slots`` frees out-of-window SWA blocks on the
processed-token basis, ``max(0, computed - in_flight)``, before every allocation):

* Every group holds at most ``cdiv(computed + new + lookahead, block_size)`` blocks
  (blocks are a prefix of the sequence, minus the freed ones).
* Before its first post-prefill allocation (prefill phase, including the time a
  finished prefill sits hidden while the Neuron scheduler runs other prefills),
  computed + new <= P + K * d, where P is the prompt length and d the tokens per
  decode step. This is the *prefill-phase* bound.
* Afterwards a SWA group holds at most the window, the trailing retained tokens and
  the unprocessed + newly scheduled tokens (<= K * d), +1 block because the window
  need not start on a block boundary; a full-attention group grows to
  ``cdiv(min(P + M + K * d, max_model_len), block_size)``. This is the
  *decode-phase* bound.

The SWA groups shrink before the full-attention group grows, so the per-request
peak is ``max(prefill-phase total, decode-phase total)``, not the sum of per-group
maxima. If the scheduler admits only while the sum of these peaks over all live
requests fits the usable pool, no ``allocate_slots`` call can fail, so no request
is preempted.

With VLLM_NEURON_SWA_EARLY_FREE=1 the scheduler frees a request's out-of-window
SWA blocks as soon as its prefill output is processed (instead of at its first
decode allocation, which the Neuron scheduler can postpone for many steps while it
hides decodes behind other prefills), and from then on charges that request only
the decode-phase bound (``phase_charge``). With N live requests of which k_p are
still in the prefill phase, admission is then
``(N - k_p) * decode + k_p * prefill <= usable``.

This module imports nothing from vLLM so the arithmetic can be checked on any CPU.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass


def cdiv(a: int, b: int) -> int:
    return -(-a // b)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class GroupDesc:
    """One KV cache group, reduced to what the bound needs.

    kind: "swa" (plain sliding window) or "full" (holds every block until the
        request finishes).
    upstream_blocks: vLLM's per-request block charge for the group
        (``cdiv(spec.max_memory_usage_bytes(cfg), spec.page_size_bytes)``); the real
        bound is clamped to it, so it can never exceed the upstream charge.
    ring_blocks: VLLM_NEURON_SWA_RING only (0 = off). A "swa" group then holds at
        most this many blocks in every phase (``swa_ring.hold_blocks``) and frees
        none before the request ends.
    """

    kind: str
    block_size: int
    upstream_blocks: int
    sliding_window: int = 0
    extra_retained_tokens: int = 0
    ring_blocks: int = 0


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AdmissionParams:
    groups: tuple
    num_blocks: int
    usable_blocks: int
    max_model_len: int
    max_concurrent_batches: int
    decode_tokens: int
    lookahead_tokens: int

    @property
    def upstream_blocks_per_request(self) -> int:
        return sum(g.upstream_blocks for g in self.groups)

    @property
    def legacy_cap(self) -> int:
        w = self.upstream_blocks_per_request
        return self.num_blocks // w if w > 0 else 0


def make_params(
    groups,
    num_blocks: int,
    max_model_len: int,
    max_concurrent_batches: int,
    decode_tokens: int = 1,
    lookahead_tokens: int = 0,
    watermark_blocks: int = 0,
) -> AdmissionParams:
    # One block of the pool is vLLM's null block; the watermark is kept free.
    return AdmissionParams(
        groups=tuple(groups),
        num_blocks=num_blocks,
        usable_blocks=num_blocks - 1 - watermark_blocks,
        max_model_len=max_model_len,
        max_concurrent_batches=max(1, max_concurrent_batches),
        decode_tokens=max(1, decode_tokens),
        lookahead_tokens=max(0, lookahead_tokens),
    )


def _in_flight(p: AdmissionParams) -> int:
    return p.max_concurrent_batches * p.decode_tokens + p.lookahead_tokens


def prefill_phase_blocks(p: AdmissionParams, prefill_len: int) -> int:
    tokens = min(prefill_len + _in_flight(p), p.max_model_len)
    total = 0
    for g in p.groups:
        blocks = cdiv(tokens, g.block_size)
        if g.kind == "swa" and g.ring_blocks:
            blocks = min(blocks, g.ring_blocks)
        total += min(blocks, g.upstream_blocks)
    return total


def decode_phase_blocks(p: AdmissionParams, final_len: int) -> int:
    full_tokens = min(final_len + _in_flight(p), p.max_model_len)
    total = 0
    for g in p.groups:
        if g.kind == "swa" and g.ring_blocks:
            # Ring: the group holds its first ring_blocks blocks to the end.
            blocks = min(cdiv(full_tokens, g.block_size), g.ring_blocks)
        elif g.kind == "swa":
            swa_tokens = min(
                g.sliding_window - 1 + g.extra_retained_tokens + _in_flight(p),
                full_tokens,
            )
            blocks = cdiv(swa_tokens, g.block_size) + 1
        else:
            blocks = cdiv(full_tokens, g.block_size)
        total += min(blocks, g.upstream_blocks)
    return total


def request_peak_blocks(p: AdmissionParams, prefill_len: int, final_len: int) -> int:
    """Upper bound on the blocks one request holds at any time, all groups.

    prefill_len: tokens its (next) prefill covers -- the prompt, or every token
        so far for a preempted request that must re-prefill.
    final_len: prompt + max_tokens (clamped to max_model_len inside).
    """
    return max(prefill_phase_blocks(p, prefill_len), decode_phase_blocks(p, final_len))


def phase_charge(
    p: AdmissionParams, prefill_len: int, final_len: int, swa_freed: bool
) -> int:
    """Admission charge for one request, by phase (VLLM_NEURON_SWA_EARLY_FREE).

    swa_freed: the request's prefill output has been processed, no prefill
        tokens are still in flight, and its out-of-window SWA blocks were freed
        right away (``NeuronScheduler._swa_early_free``). From then on it never
        holds more than the decode-phase bound, so that is its charge. Otherwise
        the charge is the unchanged ``request_peak_blocks``.
    """
    if swa_freed:
        return decode_phase_blocks(p, final_len)
    return request_peak_blocks(p, prefill_len, final_len)


def uniform_cap(p: AdmissionParams, prompt_len: int, max_tokens: int) -> int:
    """Concurrent requests of one shape that fit the usable pool (log / tests)."""
    w = request_peak_blocks(p, prompt_len, prompt_len + max_tokens)
    return p.usable_blocks // w if w > 0 else 0
